title: Peripheral artery disease: stage, side and ulcer
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's peripheral artery disease and any related ulcer.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up of left foot ulcer.

HPI
(Copied Forward): Patient is a 57-year-old female presenting for evaluation of a non-healing arterial ulcer on the top of the left foot. The patient reports a history of atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. She notes the wound has been present for several months with minimal improvement in size.

(Update): The patient returns today for a follow-up on the left foot ulceration. She reports that the wound remains stable in size but has not shown significant healing since the last visit. She denies any new systemic symptoms or acute pain changes.

Vitals: BP 128/82, HR 74, SpO2 98% on room air, Temp 98.6 F.

Review of Systems
Constitutional: Negative
Integumentary: Positive (ulcer)
Musculoskeletal: Negative
Neurological: Negative
Cardiovascular: Negative
Respiratory: Negative
Gastrointestinal: Negative
Genitourinary: Negative

Medication List
- Lisinopril 10mg daily
- Atorvastatin 40mg daily
- Aspirin 81mg daily

Exam
General: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
Skin: Examination of the left lower extremity reveals atherosclerosis of the native leg arteries. There is a non-healing arterial ulcer located on the top of the left foot. The surrounding skin is dry and pale. No drainage noted today.

Assessment
1. Atherosclerosis of the native left leg arteries.
2. Non-healing ulcer of the left foot.

Plan
1. Continue current medications for cardiovascular management.
2. Wound care: Continue local dressing changes to the left foot ulceration.
3. Follow-up in 4 weeks for wound assessment.

Electronically signed,
S. Patel, NP
October 14, 2026
explanations: Atherosclerosis of native arteries of the left leg with ulceration of the foot (HCC 263), plus the ulcer code: I70.245.
I70.24- says to use an additional code for the ulcer's site and severity: L97.529 (other part of left foot, severity not documented).

distractors.why: Ulceration is documented: it is the highest stage (HCC 263).
Use an additional code (L97.-) to identify the ulcer.

hccs.label: Atherosclerosis of Arteries of the Extremities with Ulceration or Gangrene

dropped.label: Chronic Ulcer of Skin/Except Pressure/Not Specified as Through to Bone or Muscle
